To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of a large library of antibody fragments, combined with a high throughput screening system, can lead to the isolation of antibodies with high affinity, stability and potency.

the antibody libraries and screening techniques described here can be used for selection of antibody fragments with virtually any specificity, and that the selected antibody fragments can be converted into full length antibodies with high affinity, specificity and stability.

(1) the antibody repertoire of a single human can be used to isolate a large number of mAb specific for a single target; (2) the human immune system can generate antibodies with very high affinity; (3) antibodies with high affinity can be isolated from a single human; (4) the human immune response to an antigenic challenge is very complex;
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new technologies for antibody discovery.
the discovery of human monoclonal antibodies with high affinity for a given target and with the development of antibody based therapeutics.
the development and application of recombinant technologies to produce and select human antibodies with desired binding characteristics and specificity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antibody library technology is now a mature technology that is able to generate a large number of antibodies with a high diversity of specificities and affinities.
the antibody library technologies and their application have been and will continue to be a major driver for the development of new and improved therapeutic antibodies.
recombinant antibodies are now a reality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
recombinant antibody technology has become a powerful tool for the discovery of novel antibody based therapeutics and diagnostics.

we have been successful in the development of new antibody library technologies and selection methods that allow us to generate human antibodies against virtually any target, with high affinity, specificity and potency.
the antibody discovery process is now fully under the control of the researcher.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the recombinant antibody technology will continue to develop at a rapid pace.
it is now possible to select antibodies with virtually any desired specificity from a large library.
the selection of recombinant antibodies is not a black box, and that it is possible to control and direct the outcome of selections.
